paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive disorder of thrombopoietin (THPO) production. It is characterized by severe thrombocytopenia with markedly reduced bone marrow megakaryocytes, which may progress to trilineage bone marrow failure resembling aplastic anemia (Seo et al., 2017; Pecci et al., 2018). Because the defect lies in a cytokine produced outside the hematopoietic system, the marrow failure does not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, whereas affected individuals have responded to THPO receptor agonists (Seo et al., 2017; Pecci et al., 2018; Capaci et al., 2023).

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported a boy born to Egyptian first-cousin parents who presented at 3.5 years of age with ecchymotic patches. He had very severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3 x 10(9)/l), hyporegenerative anemia, and severe neutropenia, with normal platelet size and no cytomorphologic abnormalities. Bone marrow was hypocellular with very rare immature megakaryocytes and a normal karyotype. After Fanconi anemia and PNH were excluded, he was diagnosed with idiopathic aplastic anemia. He went on to have recurrent major hemorrhages (epistaxis, gum and rectal bleeding) and severe infections that required repeated transfusions. Examination also showed preauricular skin tags and a left divergent squint. His 2 younger sibs were also affected. A brother had severe isolated thrombocytopenia (26 x 10(9)/l) at 7 months, with markedly fewer bone marrow megakaryocytes, and developed recurrent spontaneous bleeding requiring platelet transfusions at 1.6 years. A sister developed a hematoma at a vaccination site at 2 months and had anemia and severe thrombocytopenia. The parents had normal blood counts. Pecci et al. (2018) noted that thrombocytopenia was the only feature present in all patients and suggested that the trilineage aplasia in the oldest sib indicated that the disease worsens with age, making the presentation indistinguishable from CAMT due to MPL mutations.

paragraphs.text: In 3 sibs from a consanguineous Egyptian family with CAMT, Pecci et al. (2018) found no MPL variant but identified a homozygous c.355C-T transition in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution. The parents were heterozygous. The variant was absent from the SNP, 1000 Genomes, and ExAC databases. Residue R119 (R98 in the mature protein) lies in helix C of the MPL-binding domain and is highly conserved, including in EPO. In HEK293T cells, wildtype and R119C THPO were expressed and equally stable, but the THPO concentration in R119C supernatants was about 23-fold lower than wildtype, indicating defective secretion. paragraphs.text: In a boy from a consanguineous Palestinian family with CAMT, Capaci et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.-323C-T substitution in the promoter region of the THPO gene, 45 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site of transcript variant 1, by whole-exome sequencing. Both parents and a younger sib were heterozygous, and 2 healthy sibs were homozygous wildtype; the heterozygous mother had mild thrombocytopenia. The variant was absent from gnomAD. The variant abolished predicted ETS1 and STAT4 binding sites; a mutant promoter-driven luciferase reporter showed almost 80% less activity than wildtype in HEK293T cells, and chromatin immunoprecipitation showed reduced binding of both factors, significantly impaired at least for STAT4.
